channel.title: The Albert Lea Tribune - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Albert Lea Tribune (albertleatribune.com)

item.title: County attorney: No charges to be filed in rural Alden shooting
item.description: No charges will be filed against the rural Alden man who shot and killed his 45-year-old son in September in self defense as his son attacked his family, Freeborn County Attorney David Walker said Friday.

item.title: Minnesota farmers, companies hope ruling brings relief
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump’s global tariffs, which have caused mass disruption for Minnesota businesses, farmers and consumers.

item.title: Administrator's Corner: Why parent-teacher conferences matter more than ever
item.description: As the school year moves forward, families and schools have an important opportunity to strengthen one of the most powerful partnerships in a child’s education: the connection between home and school.

item.title: Star Class: How the Earth changes
item.description: Sibley Elementary School fourth graders have been learning about rocks and how the Earth changes over time.

item.title: BWSR accepting applicants for water quality grants
item.description: The Minnesota Board of Water and Soil Resources (BWSR) is now accepting grant applications for the Clean Water Legacy Partners Program, which seeks to protect, enhance and restore water quality throughout the state.

item.title: ACT announces auditions for ‘Father of the Bride’
item.description: Albert Lea Community Theatre (ACT) this week announced auditions will be Monday and Tuesday for “Father of the Bride” at the Marion Ross Performing Arts Center, 147 N. Broadway in Albert Lea.

item.title: New Year Sweepstakes winner
item.description: Susan Olson claimed her prizes for the New Year Sweepstakes on Tuesday at the Tribune.

item.title: Senate Report: Priorities for the Minnesota legislative session ahead
item.description: The 2026 legislative session kicked off on Tuesday. Much has happened since we last adjourned.

item.title: April Jeppson: Learning to problem solve and collaborate
item.description: My sixth grader joined robotics this year. Before their first competition, there was a lot of uncertainty. The robot technically worked, but “worked” is a generous term. It moved a little bit. It existed. But I will say, this momma was crazy proud that they built a robot and got it to move.
